Character_dialogue: I got nothing, sir. No sign of Niobe or Ghost. Nothin’ but blue pills.
Should we jack in and try to contact them?
It wouldn’t matter. My gut says they’re down.
No. If that ship can still fly, then we need it.
I was afraid you were gonna say that.
Search every pipe, every hole, every crack we know. Sweep as wide as possible, as fast as possible.
Captain, these lines are crawling with calamari.
Then the sooner we find them the better.
Thought you could use something to eat.
He’s going to be fine, at least until he wakes up.
The Captain has some questions for him. He better have some good answers. You see these cuts? I think they’re self-inflicted.
VDTs, maybe. I don’t know. But like I said, the answer had better be good.
Roland. I’d like to run another search through the Matrix.
How can he be in the Matrix, sir? He’s not plugged in.
This is what keeps bothering me.
His neural patterns don’t read like someone who’s in a coma. The strange thing is, I see these patterns all the time.
The big bubkis. Nada. He’s not in there.
Based on the point of entry and the [past] speed it looks like the machines will be inside of Zion in just under 20 hours.

All right, let’s move with a purpose. AK, get upstairs, I want you on holographics. [Colt,] Mauser, I want forward and aft guns manned at all times. And make sure we are running on as few pads as possible.
Hey. Hey! We got a call. Operator. It’s Seraph.
I bring word from the Oracle. You must come at once.
My name is Sati. Your name is Neo. My papa says you’re not supposed to be here. He says you must be lost. Are you lost, Neo?
That’s where the Train goes. That’s where we’re going. But you cannot go with us.
The Trainman. *whispers* I don’t like him, but my Papa says we have to do what the Trainman says or he will leave us here for ever and ever.
Morpheus, Trinity. Thank you for coming. One thing I’ve learned in all my years is that nothing ever works out just the way you want it to.
I’m the Oracle. I wish there was an easier way to get through this but there ain’t. I’m sorry this had to happen. I’m sorry I couldn’t be sitting here like you remember me. But it wasn’t meant to be.
I made a choice, and that choice cost me more than I wanted it to.

To help you to guide Neo. Now, since the real test for any choice is having to make the same choice again, knowing full well what it might cost – I guess I feel pretty good about that choice, ’cause here I am, at it again.
Do you know what happened to Neo?

Yes. He’s trapped in a place between this world and the machine world. The link is controlled by a program called the Trainman. He uses it to smuggle programs in and out of the Matrix. If he finds out where Neo is before you get to him, then I’m afraid our choices are going to become difficult.
Because of who the Trainman works for.
He has placed a bounty on your lives. You must be careful at all times. Seraph knows how to find the Trainman, he will go with you. For years, he has protected me. I hope he can do the same for you.
I know, Morpheus. I can see you’re filled with doubt, clouded by uncertainty.
After everything that’s happened, how can you expect me to believe you?

I don’t. I expect just what I’ve always expected. For you to make up your own damn mind. Believe me or don’t. All I can really tell you is your friend’s in trouble and he needs your help. He needs all our help.
Yes. No. I mean, I was.
I had to leave my home too.
Sati! Come here, darling. Leave the poor man in peace.
I’m sorry, she is still very curious.
Yes, in the restaurant at the Frenchman’s. I am Rama-Kandra. This is my wife Kamala, my daughter Sati. We are most honoured to meet you.
Oh, yes. I’m the power plant systems manager for recycling operations. My wife is an interactive software programmer, she is highly creative.
What are you doing here? You do not belong here.
Kamala! Goodness, I apologize. My wife can be very direct.
It’s okay. I don’t have an answer. I don’t even know where ‘here’ is.
This place is nowhere. It is between your world and our world.
Why’d I know you were going to say that?
The Frenchman does not forget and he does not forgive.
I know only what I need to know. I know that if you want to take something from our world into your world that does not belong there, you must go to the Frenchman.
Is that what you’re doing here?
I do not want to be cruel, Kamala. He may never see another face for the rest of his life.
I’m sorry. You don’t have to answer that question.

No. I don’t mind. The answer is simple. I love my daughter very much. I find her to be the most beautiful thing I’ve ever seen. But where we are from, that is not enough. Every program that is created must have a purpose; if it does not, it is deleted. I went to the Frenchman to save my daughter. You do not understand.
No, it is a word. What matters is the connection the word implies. I see that you are in love. Can you tell me what you would give to hold on to that connection?
Then perhaps the reason you’re here is not so different from the reason I’m here.
Get away! Get away from me!
I can’t help you. No one can help you!
It’s already late. It’s not like the Trainman to be late.
You think it has something to do with me?
I cannot say. Who knows such things? Only the Oracle.
Everyone knows the Oracle. I consulted with her before I met with the Frenchman. She promised she would look after Sati after we said goodbye.
Goodbye? You’re not staying with her?
It is not possible. Our arrangement with the Frenchman was for our daughter only. My wife and I must return to our world.

Karma’s a word. Like ‘love.’ A way of saying ‘what I am here to do.’ I do not resent my karma – I’m grateful for it. Grateful for my wonderful wife, for my beautiful daughter. They are gifts. And so I do what I must do to honour them.
Can I carry that for you?
I know you. So that’s what they wanted.
I need to get back. I’ll pay you anything you want.
One way or another I’m getting on this train
Oh, no, no, no. You’re gonna stay right here until the Merovingian says different. If I know him, you’re gonna be here for a long, long time.
I don’t want to hurt you.
You don’t get it. I built this place. Down here I make the rules. Down here I make the threats. Down here, I’m God. *to Rama-Kandra* Get on the train, or you’ll stay here with him.
We should return to the Oracle. She’ll know what to do.
No. We know what has to be done.
I get it. You must be ready to die.
I need to speak with him.
The only way you’re getting through this door is over my big dead ass.
There are no weapons allowed in the club. At the bottom of this elevator, there is a coat check girl. And if we’re lucky, one man for checking guns.
Can I take your… oh my God.
What in the hell? *laughs* I don’t believe this.

*to the DJ* Hey. Hey! *to Seraph* The prodigal child returns. L’ange sans ailes (Trans: The angel without wings). Are you here for the bounty, Seraph? *laughs heartily* Tell me, how many bullets are there in those guns? I don’t know, but I don’t think you have enough.
Oh yes, I’m sure you do, you have fought through hell to do so, yes? I’ll tell you what I’ll do. Put down the guns and I will promise you safe passage out of here.

*laughs* Quelle bonne surprise, n’est pas? (Trans: What a fine surprise, isn’t it?) Who could’ve guessed we’d all be seeing each other so soon after our last meeting? A fate too kind. And since you, my little Judas, have […] here, I can only surmise that the fortune teller has found herself another shell? Disappointing, but not unexpected. I do hope, however, she has the good manners to learn her lesson, and to remember that there is no action without consequence. And if you take something from me you will pay the price.
You know why we are here.

*laughs* Come, now. What kind of question is this? Of course I know. It’s my business to know. Some might think this a strange coincidence, but I do not. I am curious, though, as to how it actually happened. Do you know?
No? I didn’t think so. But it is always best to ask.
We want to make a deal.

*laughs* Always straight to business, huh, Morpheus? Okay. I have something you want. To make a deal, you must have something I want, yes? And it so happens there is something I want. Something I’ve wanted ever since I first came here. It is said they cannot be taken, they can only be given.

I have told you before, there’s no escaping the nature of the universe. It is that nature that has again brought you to me. Where some see coincidence, I see consequence. Where others see chance, I see cost. Bring me the eyes of the Oracle, and I will give you back your saviour. That seems a particularly fair and reasonable deal to me. Yes, no?
I don’t have time for this shit.
You want to make a deal, how about this? You give me Neo, or we all die right here, right now.
Interesting deal. You are really ready to die for this man?
She’ll do it. If she has to, she’ll kill every one of us. She’s in love.
It is remarkable how similar the pattern of love is to the pattern of insanity.
Time’s up. What’s it gonna be, Merv?
Ok. You got yourself into this. You can get yourself out.
Almost, sir. They got some pretty ancient hacks here, we’re working on it. Did you find Neo?
No, sir. We were reading something but I couldn’t tell what it was.
That’s it. That’s the secret. You’ve got to use your hands.
Cookies need love like everything does.
I was hoping to have these done before you got here. Oh well. Sati, honey, I think it’s time for a tasting. Take the bowl to Seraph and find out if they’re ready.
Okay. *to Neo* I’m glad you got out.
Yeah, that’s how it works. Some bits you lose, some bits you keep. I don’t yet recognize my face in the mirror, but… I still love candy. *offers Neo a piece of red candy*
Remember what you were like when you first walked through my door, jittery as a junebug? And now just look at you. You sure did surprise me, Neo, and you still do.
You gave me a few surprises, too.
You helped me to get here, but my question is why? Where does this go? Where does it end?
You don’t know or you won’t tell me?
I told you before. No one can see beyond a choice they don’t understand, and I mean no one.
It doesn’t matter. It’s my choice. I have mine to make, same as you have yours.
Does that include what things to tell me and what not to tell me?
Then why didn’t you tell me about the Architect? Why didn’t you tell me about Zion, the Ones before me – why didn’t you tell me the truth?
Because it wasn’t time for you to know.
You know who. *She points at the Temet Nosce sign above the door*
I did. *Oracle nods* Then I think it’s time for me to know a few more things.
Tell me how I separated my mind from my body without jacking in. Tell me how I stopped four sentinels by thinking it. Tell me just what the hell is happening to me.
The power of the One extends beyond this world. It reaches from here all the way back to where it came from.
The Source. That’s what you felt when you touched those Sentinels. But you weren’t ready for it. You should be dead, but apparently you weren’t ready for that, either.
The Architect told me that if I didn’t return to the Source, Zion would be destroyed by midnight tonight.
*rolls eyes* Please… You and I may not be able to see beyond our own choices, but that man can’t see past any choices.
He doesn’t understand them – he can’t. To him they are variables in an equation. One at a time each variable must be solved and countered. That’s his purpose: to balance an equation.
I want the same thing you want, Neo. And I am willing to go as far as you are to get it.
The end of the war. *Oracle nods* Is it going to end?
I’m sorry, I don’t have the answer to that question, but if there’s an answer, there’s only one place you’re going to find it.
You know where. And if you can’t find the answer, then I’m afraid there may be no tomorow for any of us.
Everything that has a beginning has an end. I see the end coming. I see the darkness spreading. I see death. And you are all that stands in his way.
*nods* Very soon he’s going to have the power to destroy this world, but I believe he won’t stop there; he can’t. He won’t stop until there’s nothing left at all.
He is you. Your opposite, your negative, the result of the equation trying to balance itself out.
What if I can’t stop him?
One way or another, Neo, this war is going to end. Tonight, the future of both worlds will be in your hands… or in his.
How are you feeling? Are you all right?
Good. Maybe he’s got some answers.
Mmm, I love that smell. I sure am gonna miss it.
I know, I know. Sati, honey! Take a few cookies and go with Seraph.
Can I come back? I would like to come back!
I hope so, honey, I hope so.
Well, well, it’s been a long time. I remember chasing you was like chasing a ghost.
That’s true, but as you can see, things are a little different now. *to Sati* And you must be the last exile.
The Oracle told me about you.
Really? And what did she say about me?
Oh, I’m not so bad once you get to know me.

The great and powerful Oracle. We meet at last. I suppose you’ve been expecting me, right? The all-knowing Oracle is never surprised. How can she be, she knows everything. But If that’s true, then why is she here? If she knew I was coming, why didn’t she leave? *sweeps plate of cookies off table* Maybe you knew I was going to do that, maybe you didn’t. If you did, that means you baked those cookies and set that plate right there deliberately, purposefully. Which means you’re sitting there also deliberately, purposefully.
What did you do with Sati?
Cookies need love like everything does.
Do what you’re here to do.
I really wish I could help, but I just… I don’t remember any of it.
What about the cuts on your arms? Those cuts are more than one day old.

Yeah, definitely. You’re right about that, sir. They look like they might be self-inflicted. Why would I do something like that to myself? Unless, of course, I wasn’t myself… but… if I’m not me, then who am I?
Has this man been tested for VDTs?
Yes, sir, it was negative. But he is showing a lot of unusual neural activity. Some cross-synaptic firing as well as signs of recent trauma, with fresh fibrotic scarring throughout the cortex.
I want the truth, I don’t care what it takes. Make him remember.
‘Bout time we had some goddamn good news.
Are the thermals picking up any signs of life?
Well, [holo]graphic says the hull is still intact.
Get a full diagnostic on that ship as fast as humanly possible.
Careful, sir! The squids are sneaky bastards. Could be a trap.
You can put that shit away, boys. All she needs is a jump.
Yes, I’m fine. We didn’t know what happened out here. I’m sorry.
It’s okay. I’m happy to see you too. Did you get Neo out?
Yes. How did you know about that?
Just before the sentinels found us.
The same thing she always does. Exactly what I needed to hear.

In less than 12 hours, the machines will breach the dock walls. Every simulation we’ve run, we’ve seen that once the machines are inside the city the odds of our survival decrease dramatically. Thus our primary objective must be to destroy or disable the diggers inside the dock. If we can do that, perhaps we can prevent them from ever reaching the city. If not, the only place we’ll be able to mount an effective defense will be at the entrance of the Temple. It is small enough that it will force them into a bottleneck, allowing us to concentrate the remainder of our defense.
We understand that you’ve requested additional volunteers.
Precisely what size of force are you planning to commit to the primary dock objective?
Right now, the entire APU core and half the infantry.
If it were up to me, Councillor, I’d take every man, woman, and child, put a gun in their hands and march them straight into that dock.
Perhaps it is best that it is not up to you.
Commander, just one more question. Has there been word from the Nebuchadnezzar?
None, and at this point there’s no reason to expect that there ever will be.
I’m afraid hope is an indulgence I don’t have time for.
They’re evacuating our level. We have to go.
They’ve called for volunteers to hold the dock.
*to the kids* Kids, you stay here. *to Zee* I know how you feel, Zee, but you can’t do that.
Because I love him. [I love him the same as] he loves me. And if I were out there and he were here, I know he would be doing the same thing.
But you’re gonna get yourself killed. It’s crazy, Zee.
Maybe it is. But ask yourself, if it were Dozer, and you knew the only chance you had to see him again was to hold the dock, what would you do?
What the shit is going on over here?
An accident, sir! I didn’t see… I’m sorry!
What’s a pod-born pencil-neck like you doin’ volunteering for my corps?
I want to do my part, sir! We gotta hold the dock.
Shoulda said sixteen, I mighta believed that!
Minimal age for the corps is eighteen, sixteen’s too young!
The machines won’t care how old I am. They’ll kill me just the same.
Give me a chance, sir. I won’t let you down.
You do… you’ll find me and the machines have something in common.
You want us to patch an uplink to reload the operations software, Sparky?
Yeah, that’d be swell. You can clean the windshield while you’re at it. Uplinks are in place, I’m bringing her back online. Looking good, except, uh… something wrong with the Matrix feed.
No, there’s not. You’re looking at what we’re looking at.
What the hell’s going on in there?
Whatever it is, it can’t be good.

The machines have taken Junction 21. They way I see it, if we drop down from broadcast here, [at RC153], we might surprise them. We go first, hammer as deep as we can, them blow our EMP. Hopefully, we can punch a hole big enough for you to get through.
It ain’t pretty, but the way I see it, it’s the only way back.
No it’s not. There’s another way. A support line. It drops down right here. A thousand meters short of 21. If we’re lucky, we may be able to slip down without them ever knowing.
That’s a mechanical line. It’s impossible, no one can pilot mechanical.
That was a long time ago, Niobe.
I said I can do it.
So what? If you can, you’ll be the only one that can. There’s no way we can follow you.
Hi. I know time is always against us, and I’m sorry I took so long. But I wanted to be sure.
I know what I have to do.
There’s no easy way to say this, so I’ll just say it. I have to take one of the ships.
I know it’s difficult to understand…
No, it’s not – you’re out of your goddamn mind.
You’ll never make it. hundred years no ship has gone within a hundred kilometers of it, you’ll never make it.
Is this what the Oracle told you?
This is asinine! If you want to kill yourself, go do it, but do it without wasting one of our ships.
You have to believe me, I have to go.
Bullshit! While I’m captain of this ship, I say where it has to go. Believe me, this ship will go to hell long before I let you take it anywhere.
Don’t even think of trying to tell me what I can or cannot do with my ship after that little speech.
I’ll pilot this ship. He can take mine. If we leave inside an hour, we should reach Zion as the machines do. That’s as good a plan as any.
It’s a waste. A goddamn waste.
Two ships, two directions. Sounds like providence, doesn’t it, Morpheus?
You’ve never believed in The One.
Then why are you doing this?
To help you relax. To make it easier for you to remember.
What if I don’t want to remember?
What if I blew that EMP? What if I did destroy those ships and I am responsible for the deaths of all those men? If I did that, it wouldn’t be very safe for me here, would it?
Of course, it might not be very safe for you, either.
Trinity… There’s something I have to say. Something you need to understand. I know I’m supposed to go. But beyond that – I don’t know…
I know. You don’t think you’re coming back. I knew it the moment you said you had to leave. I could see it in your face. Just like you knew the moment you looked at me that I was coming with you.

So am I. Took me ten minutes to buckle up one boot. But I’ll tell you something. Six hours ago I told the Merovingian that I was ready to give anything and everything for you. Do you know what’s changed in the past 6 hours?
Are you finished loading that amunition?
Let’s move it, we are out of time.
*hugs Trinity* I ain’t saying goodbye. I’m saying good luck.
I can only hope you know what you’re doing.
Me, too. It was an honour, sir.
‘Bout damn time. *to Niobe* We’re already late, Captain, so let’s hit it and hit it hard.
Bye, baby. Take good care of them.
Engine’s still firing. Must be a fuse. I’ll check it out.
I should’ve known he’d sent his bitch first.

No one ever got away from me as many times as you did. Every single time I thought it was the last. Every time I was sure we had you, but somehow you’d slip through our fingers. I really can’t express just how aggravating that can be.
I think I might enjoy killing you as much as killing him.
Captain, we’ve got an emergency down here.
It’s Maggie, sir. She’s dead. Murdered. I think it was Bane.
I knew it. I knew he was out of his goddamn mind. He fired that EMP. Goddamn it, I should have beaten it out of him.
We’ve searched the whole ship, captain. He ain’t here.
You don’t know that, what if they need our help!
Because if he’s killed them, he’ll control another EMP.
At this point, they’re on their own… just like us.
Mr. Anderson. I see you’re as predictable in this world as you are in the other.

It might appear that way to you, but Mr. Anderson and I know that appearances can be deceiving. Confused, Mr. Anderson? It’ll all become clear in a moment. Now, thank you for bringing me the gun. You can set it down right there.
Don’t do it. Shoot. Shoot now.
Yes, shoot, fry us, burn us alive!
Shoot, Neo. If you don’t, he’ll kill us both.
Look at him. He knows he should do it but he won’t. He can’t.
Back away from the gun and turn around.
[Somehow familiar, isn’t it?]. We’ve been here before, you and I. Remember? I do. I think of nothing else.

Still don’t recognize me? I admit, it is difficult to think, encased in this rotting piece of meat. The stink of it filling every breath, a suffocating cloud you can’t escape. *spits blood* Disgusting! Look at how pathetically fragile it is. Nothing this weak is meant to survive.
Yes.. That’s it, Mr. Anderson. Look past the flesh, look through the soft gelatin of these dull cow eyes and see your enemy.
There’s nowhere I can’t go, there’s nowhere I won’t find you.
Not impossible. Inevitable. Goodbye, Mr. Anderson.
This is it, it’s gotta’ be. {She pushes a circuit breaker, the lights go out}
I wish you could see yourself, Mr. Anderson. The blind messiah. You’re a symbol for all of your kind, Mr. Anderson. Helpless, pathetic. Just waiting to be put out of your misery.
It’s not over, Mr. Anderson. It’s not over.
I’ll be okay. It’s all right, Trin. But I think you’re gonna have to drive.
Seismic’s projecting twenty-two minutes to breach.
They can’t know we don’t have any EMP, they’ll have to attack in waves. Concentrate our offense on the diggers. Order the APUs into position.

All right, this is it. Now, you all know me, so I’ll just say this as simple as I can. If it’s our time to die, it’s our time. All I ask is: if we have to give these bastards our lives, we give ’em hell before we do!
Shit, yeah. I’ll make you a deal, though. You keep loadin’, I keep shootin’.
[Holy Christ would you look at that?]
Ghost, cut the auxilliary systems […] Switch to full manual, drop down to four pads.
If I can just get close enough.
Give me full power, full systems!
Ghost, you’re the best gunner we have, go with them. Morpheus, take his place!
Hold on to your lunch, [Roland,] here we go.
Damn. Didn’t know this ship could do that.
Where the hell’s my infantry? I want that goddamn machine taken down!
[…] it’s not the Logos, goddamn it.
Shit, she’s got a fat ass.
They’re going for the radio, stop ’em! {Sentinels take out radio} Shit.
Just give me one clean shot.
I got a dock load of incoming!
Sorry sir, but this is different, sir.
I think it’s one of ours.
That’s impossible […] Contact them, I want access codes.
It’s a trick. [It can’t be, it’s] a mechanical line. No one can pilot mechanical.
Holographs are confirmed. It’s the Hammer, sir.
The ship is under attack, sustaining heavy damage. But at its present velocity, it’ll reach Gate 3 in twelve minutes.
It’d take out more than that. It’d wipe out our entire defense system. […] EMP in there, we will lose the dock!
But sir, we’ve already lost the dock.
[…] critical damage, sir! [We’ve lost control! We] can’t open it!
On my mark, give me full power, 90 degrees, lower right starboard.
We ain’t home yet. What about the gate?
The sentinels are inside the dock.
Get me the one closest to Gate 3.
You have to open that gate. Cut the counterweights. […] You can do it. Hurry. There’s no time.
[…] I didn’t finish the training program.
[…] We gotta blow the EMP now!
[Light as a feather. Light as a feather.]
Commander, […] Captain Mifune’s APU is up and moving to Gate 3!
Captain Mifune’s APU’s just reached Gate 3!
Mifune, this is Lock. I don’t know if you can hear me but if you can…
…the Hammer is two minutes away […] you’ve got two minutes, Captain, to get that gate open.
You’re a hell of a pilot.
Some things in this world never change.
I knew you’d come. I knew it.
Are you kidding? I [‘m never gonna take] it off!
Three captains, one ship. I assume the other ships were lost under equally pointless circumstances?
Good to see you too, Jason.
Council’s waiting to hear an explanation. You’ll forgive me for not attending, but I have to try to salvage this debacle.
Did I miss something, Commander? I thought we just saved the dock.

That’s the problem with you people. You can’t think for five minutes in front of your face. That EMP knocked out almost every piece of hardware and every APU. If I were the machines, I would send every Sentinel I had here right now. Saved the dock, captain? You’ve just handed it to them on a silver platter.
Get that cable cut! I want that system back online.
Commander, it’s the dock. We’ve got incoming.
Order everyone to fall back. Seal the shaft. Now.
Do it. *the shaft is sealed, and he looks up* Your move.
So you gave them your ship?
That is correct, Councillor, I did.
Knowing what he planned to do with it?
And the Oracle said nothing of this?
She told me Neo would need my help, and when the time came I would choose to help him or not.
But what hope can a single vessel have against their entire defense system?
None, it’s completely impossible, but he wouldn’t listen. He wouldn’t even take any ammunition. He was totally out of his goddamn mind.

No, he wasn’t. Neo is doing what he believes he must do. I don’t know if what he’s doing is right, and I don’t know if he’ll reach the machine city. And if he does, I don’t know what he can do to save us. But I do know that as long as there’s a single breath in his body, he will not give up. And neither can we.
We’re over the fields, aren’t we?
Over there. There’s our path. Can you see it? Three lines.
What do we do now, Commander?
It is now a matter of time. The machines will breach the walls of the city. I recommend that the Council join the rest of the non-military personnel inside the Temple.
Two hours. Maybe less. My men have begun fortifying the entrance with enough artillery to make our last stand. Beyond that, there isn’t anything more I can do.
Commander, do you think that we have any chance of surviving?
If I were you, Councillor, I wouldn’t ask me that question. I would as him *motions with hand toward Morpheus*
Because he’s the one who believes in miracles.
Do you see what’s out there?
If you tell me we’ll make it, I’ll believe you.
We’ll make it. We have to.
Gotcha! Come on, Neo, I need help here!
The sky… it’s the only way.
Pump the igniter, the ship will start. Again, slowly. Now!
It’s unbelievable, Trin. Lights everywhere. Like the whole thing was built with light. I wish you could see what I see.
You’ve already shown me so much.
What is it, Trinity? What’s wrong?
